editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / The Debate Behind the Launch / What We Don't Know / Background) at 738 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Clear, neutral narration of a governance/funding story with a genuinely reported angle (the maintainer pushback in the GitHub thread) rather than a rewrite of the press release alone.
editor_notes.source_verification: 3 sources cited, all three domains (fortune.com, finance.yahoo.com, github.com) already present in config/source_allowlist.txt - no allowlist action needed. (1) fortune.com press-release snapshot (source-0.html.gz, sha256 ad4900c5...) read in full: confirms the Nov 17, 2026 launch date, initial participants (Node.js, Fastify, Lodash, webpack, jQuery, OpenJS's own site), opt-in structure, no-behavioral-tracking claim, BuySellAds/OpenJS role split, and the 'no single solution to open source sustainability' quote verbatim. (2) finance.yahoo.com snapshot failed to fetch (manifest: error 'fetch failed', file: null). No Wayback Machine capture exists for this URL (checked via archive.org/wayback/available - empty result). As a last resort, used a live WebFetch of the URL per policy; it returned the same EZ Newswire press-release text as the Fortune snapshot (syndicated copy), independently confirming the 'behavioral targeting' wording (see factual_accuracy) and the sustainability quote. Because this is the same wire release as source-0, it is NOT independent of source-0 for sourcing-diversity purposes - both ultimately originate from BuySellAds/EZ Newswire. (3) github.com/openjs-foundation/cross-project-council/issues/1797 (source-2.html.gz, sha256 f2fb862b...) read in full, including the embedded GraphQL/JSON comment data that carries each commenter's real display name. Verified real names behind GitHub handles: rginn = Robin Bender Ginn, nikwen = Niklas Wenzel, voxpelli = Pelle Wessman, tobie = Tobie Langel, rogermbyrne = identifies only as 'Roger' in his own comment text (article correctly does not supply a surname for him). suspicious_patterns is null on all three manifest entries; no injection-pattern scan hits to evaluate. Anthropic disclosure: not required - article does not mention Anthropic or an Anthropic-operated product.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Ran the claim-accuracy checks against the raw snapshot/live-fetch text rather than trusting the submission. Two verbatim-quote errors found, both subordinate (not in headline/summary/lead): (1) Article quotes the foundation as saying the network 'will not use behavioral tracking or third-party tracking.' Both the Fortune snapshot and the live Yahoo Finance fetch show the actual wording is 'will not use behavioral targeting or third-party tracking' - the writer substituted 'tracking' for 'targeting,' which both changes the meaning (ad-targeting practice vs. data-tracking practice) and produces an odd doubled 'tracking.' (2) Article quotes Tobie Langel asking for 'regular updates on how this sustainability program is going.' The raw GitHub comment text (verified via direct grep of the decompressed HTML/JSON) reads 'regular updates on how this sustainability programs are going' (plural 'programs', a grammatical slip in the original comment) - the writer silently smoothed the grammar inside a direct quote. All other direct quotes checked verbatim against source text: Ginn's Aug 1 and Sep 14 GitHub comments, Wenzel's '10x as much' argument, Roger/BuySellAds' rate-card and ad-quality quotes, and the 'no single solution to open source sustainability' quote all match the source text exactly. Absence claims verified: neither source discloses a dollar revenue figure, and the launch announcement indeed omits the 50/50 split mentioned in the August GitHub proposal - both checked against the full text of all three sources, not just the adjacent citation. Dates (Aug 1, Aug 4, Aug 25, Aug 31, Sep 14, Sep 15, Nov 17, all 2026) all confirmed against the GitHub issue's comment timestamps and the Fortune dateline. One minor unsourced-but-true detail: the article calls Robin Bender Ginn the foundation's 'executive director' - this title does not appear in any of the three cited sources (the GitHub issue only shows her as the issue author 'rginn'/'Robin Bender Ginn'; Fortune/Yahoo don't name her at all). The title is accurate per public record but is not traceable to a cited source in this submission.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The 'Debate Behind the Launch' section gives roughly equal weight to the pro-network (BuySellAds/Roger) and skeptical (Wenzel, Wessman) positions, with direct quotes from both sides rather than editorializing. No sensational language; 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags the absence of revenue figures instead of speculating.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior OpenJS coverage: three existing articles (2026-09 Node.js AI-PR governance, 2026-04 Node.js 26, 2026-05 Node.js VFS/TSC governance, 2026-05 Linux Foundation package-registries working group) concern OpenJS-ecosystem governance or releases but none cover the ad network / BuySellAds story. This is a new topic, not a duplicate.
concerns: Direct quote misquote: 'behavioral tracking' should be 'behavioral targeting' per both the Fortune press-release snapshot and a live fetch of the Yahoo Finance republication.
Direct quote misquote: Tobie Langel's quote renders 'this sustainability programs are going' (verbatim, including the grammatical slip) as 'this sustainability program is going' (silently corrected).
The 'executive director' title for Robin Bender Ginn is not sourced in any of the three cited URLs, though it is accurate.

Fortune and Yahoo Finance sources are the same syndicated EZ Newswire/BuySellAds press release, not independent outlets - acceptable for a News piece (no independent-source minimum applies, unlike Analysis) but worth noting.
recommendations: File a corrections record for the two verbatim-quote deviations (behavioral targeting/tracking; Langel's singular/plural wording).

Future submissions should re-verify direct quotes word-for-word against source text before enclosing them in quote marks, rather than lightly paraphrasing or grammar-correcting inside quotation marks.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, well-sourced News story about OpenJS's ad-network launch, with real added reporting value from the GitHub debate thread. Two isolated word-level misquotes (both subordinate, not headline/summary/lead) are honestly coverable in a single corrections note; nothing here rises to a REJECT-level pattern of fabrication or an unsourced lead claim. Featured candidacy: 0 - routine open-source-funding/governance news of interest mainly to the JS ecosystem, not broad or exceptional enough to feature.
